messages:
Alex: Heads up — us-east1 hotstripe pool is seeing NVMe IOPS saturation impacting GPU provisioning since ~00:10 UTC. A number of small-batch jobs are failing with attach timeouts. Possible overlap with janitor scrubs and nightly compaction.

infra-bot: ALERT: nvme_iops_throttle detected on pool=hotstripe-us-east1 (15% nodes degraded). Spike started at 2026-03-21T00:09:00Z. https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/8472 :warning:

Maya: saw a similar blip last week but not this large. scrub window might have drifted into peak. any quick telemetry?

Jorge: digging into node logs now. pulled a few tails:```
[00:11:42] nvme: queue_depth=256 iops_wait=380ms
[00:11:42] kernel: nvme0: I/O timeout, scheduling retry
[00:11:43] attach: ERROR attach failed: iops_quota_exceeded (code=28)
```

Priya: can we hot-fix by reducing scrub concurrency or cordoning scrub jobs for hotstripe? prioritize GPU attach success. Also are we routing to warmstripe fallback?

Alex: plan proposal: 1) temporarily set janitor/scrub concurrency -> 1 for hotstripe-us-east1 2) enable fallback routing of GPU attach to warmstripe pool for non-data-local jobs 3) increase short-term IOPS quota on 25% of critical nodes to unblock in-flight jobs 4) monitor wear metrics (we trade cost/wear for availability).

Jorge: commands I'm going to run now:```
# reduce janitor concurrency
platformctl scrub update --pool hotstripe-us-east1 --concurrency 1 --reason "mitigate IOPS surge"
# enable fallback routing for non-data-local GPU attaches
platformctl routing update --route gpu_attach --fallback warmstripe-us-east1 --filter "non-local"
```

Maya: note that bumping IOPS quota will raise cost and accelerate wear. +1 on concurrency drop and fallback. keep IOPS bump minimal.

Alex: agreed. I'll only bump by 20% on 10 nodes labeled critical. Jorge, please hold the increase until after we confirm concurrency change is applied.

infra-bot: MONITOR: scrub_concurrency_change applied to hotstripe-us-east1 by Jorge at 2026-03-21T00:18:24Z.

Jorge: scrub concurrency lowered. watching attach success rate. so far attach failures down from 18/min -> 4/min.

Priya: can we also reduce generation batch size for the next hour? that lowers per-request token bursts hitting NVMe caches.

Alex: yes — will push a temporary config to hosted-api to set `max_gen_batch=8` for us-east region for 60m. doing now.

infra-bot: CONFIG: max_gen_batch changed for region us-east (scope=hosted-api) by Alex at 2026-03-21T00:28:05Z.

Jorge: attach failure rate stabilized around 2/min. some nodes still showing elevated latency, but overall provisioning success back to normal tail.

Maya: logging this as INC-8342 and will follow up with a root-cause: scrub schedule drift + insufficient hotstripe fallback capacity during warmup.

Alex: thanks everyone. short-term mitigations in place (concurrency drop + routing fallback + batch cap). next steps: postmortem, schedule stricter scrub windows, and consider autoscale policy that pre-warms warmstripe when scrub backlog > X.

Priya: +1 on pre-warm. also add a dashboard showing scrub/scheduling overlap and gpu-attach SLO correlation.

Jorge: will keep monitoring for the next 2 hours and rollback the IOPS bump if wear signals spike.

Alex: closing thread for now — will update INC-8342 with timeline and logs. :thumbsup:
